mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up our time with Far from the Tree by Andrew Solomon, there’s one truth that really stands out—difference isn’t just something to overcome. It’s a challenge, sure, but it’s also a gift. Families don’t get to choose what kinds of difference show up in their lives. But every day, they get to decide how to respond. The stories we’ve explored are filled with moments of fear, confusion, and even grief. But alongside those, there’s incredible resilience, real growth, and a kind of love that only grows deeper when things don’t go as planned. Here’s what this means for you: No family has all the answers. Every family faces difference, and how they handle it ends up shaping their story more than anything else. Acceptance isn’t just a single decision—it’s a journey. Sometimes, it takes time, and that’s okay. Community and connection really matter. They’re what help us keep going when things get tough. And love? It’s not about everyone being the same. It’s about showing up, listening, and understanding—especially when it’s hard. When we learn to embrace what makes us and our families different, something amazing happens. We transform—not just as individuals, but together. Let’s be real: the road through difference is rarely simple. There’ll be days when you wish things were easier, when you feel alone, or just worn out. But there will also be moments of laughter, of connection, and a pride that wouldn’t exist if life had been simple. So if you’re navigating difference—whether you’re a parent, a child, or someone just trying to understand—remember, you’re not alone. The world is wider, and more generous, than it sometimes feels. By choosing to embrace difference, by reaching out for connection, and by letting go of old expectations, you’re helping to create a richer, more beautiful life—not just for yourself, but for everyone around you. This work never really ends. But the rewards? They’re absolutely real. Keep going.
